Market Correlation (2021)

In this paper I look for correlation between currency pairs, and how
it can show us the dominant Matrix. I start with how the mind
correlates, then use Goodman Wave Theory to read a race between two
pairs, EURUSD and GBPUSD.
How the mind correlates

Every day, our minds try to correlate what happened in the past, or
just a few days before, to deal with each new challenge. In every
circumstance the mind spends some time, perhaps only 10 seconds,
depending on its state and passion, to correlate and analyse. The aim is
to reach the greatest goal the circumstance allows.
That goal can be reached in only three ways: chance, logic, or both (blessing, or luck).

Figure: Three routes to the goal: chance, logic, and blessing
(luck).
Chance

With chance there is zero correlation the mind can work with. With
reason or analysis, or without them, in the end it is decided by
chance.
Logic

Logic is based on a true conclusion that correlates with its premise.
The mind can work with a high correlation here. But it meets a lot of
bad fate when the conclusion is false, and it is cold and silent when it
comes to fixing conclusions. Every mind holds a thousand false
conclusions.
Luck, or blessing

Luck is built on months and years of practice, as with football
players. The only logic is in the practice: with more practice, a chance
becomes more attainable. But there is no direct cause that achieves the
goal. It is relative logic and relative chance, so the correlations are
relative too. I prefer to call this a blessing rather than luck. It has
a direct link with the law of attraction.
The new theory of chance

The new theory of chance states that events with zero correlation can
produce a new correlation across many outcomes. Instead of seeking a
correlation from one coin flip, we find it across 100 flips. There the
mind has a lot to analyse.

The greatest inventors in history searched through many outcomes for
a definite correlation that would solve the problem. I do not mean they
used the theory of chance. But in the end, they always investigated any
correlation that could help them reach a goal.

"I have not failed. I've just found 10,000 ways that won't work."

"There are no rules here – we're trying to accomplish something."

— Thomas A. Edison

From this, I believe there are many correlations between pairs that
help us know the dominant Matrix. We need to know the correlation for
each type of circumstance. Unfortunately, there are no rules: only
investigation, with patience and passion.

Organizing the pairs by the
dollar

The forex pairs are many: EURUSD, USDJPY, GBPUSD, USDCHF, AUDUSD,
USDCAD, NZDUSD and more. To me they are a puzzle, a chessboard. With so
many pairs it is easy to lose concentration, so I organize them by
international trade.

"In addition to accounting for the bulk of global reserves, the dollar is the currency of choice for international trade. Major commodities such as oil are primarily bought and sold using U.S. dollars."

So I take EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD and NZDUSD. When these pairs rise,
the dollar falls. "If a trader goes long EUR/USD, he or she buys Euros
and sells US dollars."

When the dollar falls, the world is in trouble: its external
purchasing power drops. Anyone who saves dollars in a bank finds, over
the years, that they are worth less and less.

That is not the purpose of this study. I am looking for a dominant
trend through correlation. But it gives a strong ground to start from.
The market can only move up and down, but with the dollar's purchasing
power falling, these pairs can only move up. That is a logical
correlation: EUR, GBP, AUD and NZD all share at least one direct cause,
the dollar. Here I show a causal analysis using Goodman Theory, which
shows very clearly how purchasing power works at the different Goodman
points, in each circumstance.

The Analysis of Market Mind
(2021)

In this paper I want to show how people change their beliefs over
time, and how we can read those changes on a chart. From the changes in
belief I build a hypothesis about the near future, and then I let the
market confirm it or reject it. The first part lays the ground: price,
volume and time, demand, mental energy and the Goodman rules. The second
part puts that ground to work on theoretical charts, on a set of
correlated pairs, on real examples, and finally on a full live study of
NZDUSD.

Introduction: conflict and
belief

In every conflict, people naturally look for a way out. They do not
want the conflict; they want it to disappear. When it is intense they
cannot wait for it to end, even if it takes months.

When they see a high chance that the bad outcome will happen, they
treat it as definite fate. Then they start looking for a way through.
They know that fear is only the gate to the dark, the place of doubt and
hesitation.

So they try to believe there is a happier fate. There is a
possibility instead of the unwanted consequence, a chance for the events
they want. That good chance appears whenever there is a balance in
beliefs.

The human mind naturally weighs every premise. It tries to weaken
every conclusion that supports fearful beliefs, and it lets good beliefs
emerge by drawing new conclusions. The pages that follow explain how
people change their beliefs, and how I make a hypothesis about the near
future from those changes over time.

Ideology: what a chart
carries
A chart carries only a few pieces of data:

• Price: high, low, open and close.

  • Time: the period within which price travels.

  • Volume: the liquidity.
Logical ground

Price, volume and time as
one space

Price tells us the final negotiation between buyers and sellers
within a period. Volume describes the quantity buyers took from sellers,
or sellers gave to buyers, in that same period. The two are connected as
dependent variables. Together with time they form a kind of 3D
space.
Price shapes belief

Price affects the buyer's beliefs about the future. When the current
price is heavily discounted, sellers are reluctant to sell until price
reaches what they desire. Remember the headlines about the milk crash,
when Sardinian farmers dumped their milk in protest at prices.

This is the most exciting part of the supply and demand equation.
Buyer and seller are both dependent variables. Most of the time it works
like an auction: each side bids against the other, and the stronger side
sets the price.
The types of demand

Demand is not one thing. The standard list [Demand, Wikipedia] gives
eight states:

• Negative demand: consumers dislike the product and may even pay to avoid it.

  • Nonexistent demand: consumers may be unaware of the product or uninterested in it.

  • Latent demand: consumers may share a strong need that no existing product can satisfy.

  • Declining demand: consumers begin to buy the product less often, or not at all.

  • Irregular demand: purchases vary by season, month, week, day or even hour.

  • Full demand: consumers are adequately buying all products put into the marketplace.

  • Overfull demand: more consumers want to buy than can be satisfied.

  • Unwholesome demand: consumers may be attracted to products with undesirable social consequences.
The Mental Energy Model

Energy behind every change
in price

This model analyzes the energy behind every change in price within
the order system. Mental energy simply deals with the reaction of
belief. In the end, belief controls the space of action.

When belief is very strong, the reaction, the action, is just as
strong, but in a different direction. Belief lives in the direction of
the heart; action lives in the direction of the senses.
Goals, choices and energy

Think of a team that wants to win the World Cup final. You can see
the players energized by the goal itself. The origin of energy is the
desire to achieve a goal. Goals act directly on choices, and choices are
the key to energy.

The Nash equilibrium (after the mathematician John Forbes Nash Jr.)
deals with which strategy, which choice, is best for a player to
maximize the payoff against an opponent:

"If two players Alice and Bob choose strategies A and B, (A, B) is a Nash equilibrium if Alice has no other strategy available that does better than A at maximizing her payoff in response to Bob choosing B, and Bob has no other strategy available that does better than B at maximizing his payoff in response to Alice choosing A."

No risk, no reward. Here risk means the energy spent to maximize the
payoff inside the game.

The market as a zero-sum
game

In game theory, "a zero-sum game is a mathematical representation of
a situation in which an advantage that is won by one of two sides is
lost by the other" [Cambridge Business English Dictionary]. The market
and its financial instruments are an example. Debit and credit in
accounting show this very simply:

"The rules governing the use of debits and credits are as follows:

All accounts that normally contain a debit balance will increase in amount when a debit (left column) is added to them, and reduced when a credit (right column) is added to them. The types of accounts to which this rule applies are expenses, assets, and dividends.

All accounts that normally contain a credit balance will increase in amount when a credit (right column) is added to them, and reduced when a debit (left column) is added to them. The types of accounts to which this rule applies are liabilities, revenues, and equity.

The total amount of debits must equal the total amount of credits in a transaction. Otherwise, an accounting transaction is said to be unbalanced, and will not be accepted by the accounting software." [Debits and credits definition, accountingtools.com]
Impression force

Whenever buyers believe there is a chance, an opportunity, to reach
the maximum payoff by choosing a strategy, the goal energizes their mind
and belief. The reaction becomes more intense.

Over time that energy leaves an impression. An impression is one type
of memory. It can support energy and encourage it to reach the goal.
Energy and impression are independent variables.

The crowd at a football match supports the player: that is the
impression force, an independent variable. The player energizes himself
by the goal: that is mental energy. When the impression force is at its
maximum, it becomes like a gravity force that acts as an energy
field.

Figure: The mental energy model: goal, choice, mental energy and
action, with the impression force supporting from outside.

The Goodman rules behind the
model
Goodman Measured Move Rule

Every swing moves by percentage from 0 to 100, and the reaction
returns from 100 towards 0. This is the total progress of each buyer's
and seller's energy. When buyers seek their maximum payoff, it is
relative to the previous payoff, and that progress shows very clearly
how buyers move.
Propagation

Buyers and sellers always seek a maximum, and each maximum is
relative to the old one. They grow whenever they seek a new maximum.
Goodman Setup

Whenever the market shows a 1-2-3, the move propagates into a 1. When
price returns to around the TP of that 1, or between the EP and the SS,
it sets up the next swing in the direction of the 1-2-3. Every trade
must be qualified, and it requires at least one Propagation.
Intersection

When the market moves into an old maximum, there is almost always an
impression force there. It acts directly on today's traders who seek the
new maximum. This is the Intersection between the old and the current
maximum, and the Goodman Box shows it very clearly.
Trend

Anyone who fights the trend is fated to lose; no one can beat the
market. The trend is simply the path along which Propagation can happen.
Propagation shows the progress of the movement and of the mental
energy.

Methodology: from theory
to application

In this part I give theoretical examples that turn the ground above
into a constructive application. I start from the basics and go to the
deepest concepts.
Drawing a swing

No one can take swings into a 1-2-3 and on to Propagation without
first drawing the swing correctly; it is very hard to continue without
this. As a rule, buyers and sellers always seek their maximum. So when
you draw a swing, follow it to its extreme and then draw a line. That
line represents a wave.

Figure: A raw price chart before any drawing. Real data: AUDUSD,
2-hour, 14 February to 4 March 2022. (The original chart's symbol and
dates are not known; this one shows the same structure.)
Where are the maximum point and the minimum point?

Figure: The first swings drawn to their extremes: FPS, SS and SPS.
Real data: AUDUSD, 2-hour, 14 February to 4 March 2022. (The original
chart's symbol and dates are not known; this one shows the same
structure.)

1. The first swing runs to its maximum, the EP of the FPS.

2. The second swing runs to its maximum, the EP of the SS.

3. The third swing runs to its maximum, the EP of the SPS.

The market shows progress from 0 at the BP of the FPS to 100 at the
EP of the SPS. Now these three waves propagate into one wave, and we
test the next reaction.
The 25% rule for a reaction

When a reaction tests the entire movement, anything less than 25%
cannot count as a reaction to the whole move. It may be a reaction to
one swing, but never to the entire movement as a Propagation.

Figure: The 1-2-3 propagates into a 1, and the next swing is read as
the reaction to that 1. Real data: AUDUSD, 2-hour, 14 February to 4
March 2022. (The original chart's symbol and dates are not known; this
one shows the same structure.)

Here the 1-2-3 propagates into a 1, and the next reaction can be read
as a reaction to that 1. At this point there is a Setup signal for a
long trade, but only after qualifying the trade with inside and outside
analysis. It is stronger when an Overlay combination shows at the
extremes. Even a Dagger setup must sit within the SS of the last
Propagation, perhaps a Propagation on a higher timeframe.

Figure: The buy Setup at the reaction to the propagated 1. Real data:
AUDUSD, 2-hour, 14 February to 4 March 2022. (The original chart's
symbol and dates are not known; this one shows the same structure.)
Larger and larger cycles

Here is a larger 1-2-3; I call it a complete cycle to the upside.
Notice that on the downside there is never a complete cycle, never a
1-2-3. With Propagation you follow the trend easily, because you know
the market is simply propagating. Think in 1-2-3 with Propagation. So
let us draw it as a larger 1, and then watch the new SS.

Figure: A larger 1-2-3 completes on the upside, with a second buy at
its reaction. Real data: AUDUSD, 2-hour, 14 February to 4 March 2022.
(The original chart's symbol and dates are not known; this one shows the
same structure.)

Again a larger 1-2-3, then the next reaction. Everything in the
market fits inside the 1-2-3 and Propagation framework. So you know
everything: if the market always moves within this framework, nothing in
it is strange and nothing is new.

What follows is more logical analysis of this framework, but the
framework alone is enough. Its great advantage is that it always keeps
you with the trend, instead of thinking about reversals and always
fighting the trend.

Figure: The largest 1-2-3 propagates again, and the buy comes at the
reaction to the new 1. Real data: AUDUSD, 2-hour, 14 February to 4 March
2022. (The original chart's symbol and dates are not known; this one
shows the same structure.)
Three notes on Propagation:

1. A larger Propagation requires a larger reaction SS. 25% of a smaller Propagation is smaller than 25% of a larger one.

2. When the market comes out of a Jumbo, the new trend starts with a small Propagation that grows larger and larger. Do not forget to treat it as a Jumbo.

3. Always confirm the Propagation with Inward-Outward analysis.

Figure: Thinking in 1-2-3 with Propagation: three swings collapse
into one larger "1", and a reaction of at least 25% of the whole move is
the Setup.

Chart analysis:
reading energy box by box

This analysis is purely theoretical. It uses the 1-2-3 and the
Goodman Box with time and volume, going from uptrend to downtrend to
uptrend as one full 1-2-3 cycle.

Figure: A first swing and its reaction, with the highest volume of
each swing below.

The columns at the bottom represent volume. Simply take the highest
volume within each swing. Volume represents the intensity of belief in
reaching the maximum. What is the next swing?

By the Measured Move Rule, the first swing moves to 100%, and the
reaction swings back to 50%.

Which side has greater
energy?

You do not need to know what is happening. Our task is to know which
side has greater energy. Then we build a probability logic showing
whether the chance favors the buyers' energy or the sellers'. If we
cannot tell, we are neutral, because the chance is 50% for each
side.
In this example the chance is to move to the SPS, for four signs:

1. Buyers ended their move at 100%, while sellers ended at 50% of the buyers' swing.

2. Buyers held the swing (time) longer than sellers.

3. Volume increased on the buyers' wave and decreased on the sellers'. Buyers show more intensity.

4. The range of the FPS swing, with its volume, is relatively regular.

So the chance of an SPS and a Propagation into an uptrend is more
favorable. When there is no 1-2-3 yet, we place the box neatly around a
swing, until the chart shows a 1-2-3.

These four arguments are the premises of the hypothesis that the near
future is Propagation. The hypothesis can be false whenever the chart
does not follow it. The market confirms the hypothesis.

Figure: Four signs of energy (range, time, volume and angle),
compared box by box to see which side chance favours.
Box 3: the 1-2-3 completes

Figure: The 1-2-3 completes; box 3 gains +3 boxes above the top of
box 1.

At this point the market completes the 1-2-3. What is the chance for
the next point? Let us compare the changes in the boxes.

In box 3 the volume increased, and price gained more than three
boxes. The range of the swing is relatively regular, but not like the
old behavior in box 1; buyers fell back a little. Box 3 gains +3 boxes,
more than the box 2 reaction, so there is progress on the upswing.
Two inferences follow:

1. In box 3 buyers slowed a little, judged by the intensity of volume and by time, comparing boxes 1 and 3.

2. Buyers cancel by the 3-C. To me this does not prove they are very strong. Strong buyers must renew their energy to make a breakaway 3-C count. So the buyers are regular, but not that strong.

Where there is no intensity from sellers, the chance is only for a
reaction. We redraw a box with the 1-2-3. Watch the chart like a movie:
the energy changes between sellers and buyers, always inside the
Propagation framework.
The box propagates

Figure: The swing box propagates into a 1-2-3 box, with a green mark
above it and a buy Setup at the reaction.

The box clearly propagates, from a swing box to a 1-2-3 box. Whenever
I have a 1-2-3 box, I mark the top of it in green. It keeps me proactive
with the chart: there is a chance to propagate up to the green.

The chart confirms the last hypothesis. Volume in box 2 is lower than
in box 1. The rise in sellers' volume in box 2 is normal, because box 2
is only a test of Propagation 1. As the proportions grow larger, the
correction ratio also grows larger.

Here the chart shows a buy Setup signal. The chance favors a move to
box 3, the SPS.
Mental energy in box 3

Figure: Box 3 reaches only +3 above box 1, on a faster angle and the
lowest volume.

Let us watch the mental energy in box 3. Buyers seek their maximum
with low intensity; compare it with boxes 1 and 2. Yet that low
intensity produces a good range of swing, a good box. Box 3 gains only
+3 above box 1, but time improves: the angle is faster than in box 1.
(Box 3 can be flat or complex; box 1 was complete, and box 3 here is
flat.)
Let me summarize the facts in box 3:

• The angle is faster; buyers move more quickly than in box 1.

  • The range of box 3 is smaller than box 1.

  • Volume is lower than in box 1 or box 2.

Now let us connect these facts to deduce the relative energy. The
mental energy is very fast, the endpoint gains relatively little, and
the intensity is very low.

The move is easy (angle) with less intensity (volume). In box 1 the
intensity was high but the angle normal; there was a latent buyer, as
the high volume shows. In box 3 a small volume produces a good range,
which says buyers can rise easily with very low energy. But when I add
the Measured Move Rule, buyers are very slow in progress: just +3, then
the swing ends. This case is a little intricate.

To decide it we still need more evidence about floating supply. The
chance to resume the Propagation is lower than in the earlier case of
boxes 1 and 2, where we had the buy Setup. So the next step is the
reaction SS, and we redraw the box and lines.
Box 2 of the new cycle

Figure: The new SS falls on a very slow angle with lower volume,
while price stays inside the uptrend.

In box 2 the angle is very slow, slower than the old SS, and the
volume is lower than in box 1. We are still in an uptrend, as the green
above box 1 shows, so the chance of a Propagation to the SPS is favored.
Here is another buy opportunity, but a risky one, because the trend is
now far from the BP at the bottom of box 1.

When sellers cannot move fast, the message is that buyers' orders are
stopping them. It is a tug of war. Whenever sellers are slow, either
buyers are slowing them, or they are slow without any buyers'
orders.
The buyers withdraw

Figure: Box 3 shows very slow buyers, poor gains and heavy volume;
the gray mark shows where I take profit and turn neutral.

Here the chart shows very slow buyers with very poor gains, and also
heavy volume. It is the worst behavior of all three boxes. At this point
I take all the profit from the buy orders, as the gray mark above box 3
shows. I am neutral.

Look how the impression force can detect the buyers' withdrawal from
Propagation. Just compare the old with the new over time.

Figure: Comparing the old boxes with the new reveals the buyers'
withdrawal.

At this time, stay neutral or find other pairs to trade. Let us clean
the chart for the next analysis.
Sellers gain energy

Figure: The cleaned chart: box 2 of the decline shows better speed
and volume for sellers.

In box 2 there is some improvement in the sellers' behavior. From
what the chart tells, sellers increased their intensity, and their angle
is better than any old SS. The chart must confirm the hypothesis: buyers
cannot move above the box. The chart is moving into a Dagger.

Figure: The box becomes a Jumbo: the last buyers lose energy while
sellers gain new energy.

First, the box becomes a Jumbo. In the last box the buyers are losing
energy, while the sellers have new energy in box 2. Let us confirm it
with a 1-2-3.

Figure: A down 1-2-3 after the Jumbo turns me from neutral to
short.

Whenever I have a 1-2-3 after the Jumbo, I change from neutral to
short. The volume in the Jumbo is cancelled, because this is the new
trend.

Be careful at the change from a Jumbo to a new trend: all the volume
relations change. Only look at the higher timeframe, treat the Jumbo as
the FPS and the new trend as the SS. We must always read volume and time
within the trend structure, the Propagation, and the Overlay
combination.
Figure: The down 1-2-3 gives a Goodman Setup to the short side.

So the chance favors the downtrend. There is a Goodman Setup: short.
This is only a theoretical idea, to construct a method for trading in
real time.
Market correlation

The prerequisites for this section are Propagation and the market
analysis above. Here is a theoretical example with four pairs.

Figure: Four theoretical pairs, A to D, each with its swings and
volume.

Which one has more chance to move up, or down, or is undefined? Which
one leads the way down, or up?
From BP to EP of the FPS

In box A the FPS of the Propagation shows a good move and a good
angle, better than B and C. So from the FPS the best is A. D has no
complete cycle and no 1-2-3. Across boxes A, B and C, the best chance to
move up is A, then B; C is the slowest. D is out of the upward
correlation, but D leads the way down.
From BP to EP of the SS

Box A shows a reaction of around 50%, with more volume than in its
FPS; that keeps me on alert. Box B is healthy. Box C is on alert. So
here the chance to move up belongs to box B: the lead changes from A to
B. Meanwhile D confirms the weakness.
From BP to EP of the SPS

• Box A: volume is regular, but there is no gain.

  • Box B: volume increases, then the swing ends at the BP of the SS, with no gain.

  • Box C: volume rises abnormally, with no gain. It has the lowest gains and the worst angle of all the boxes.

All of them show some symptoms of weakness. The leader in weakness,
showing a healthy downtrend, is box D, then box C with the lowest gains,
at 50% of its SS. Just look at the FPS volume, the SPS volume and their
ranges.

So the healthiest to trade are box D, then box C. On A and B I am
neutral, because there is still a chance for them to move up.

A
live study: the minds of buyers and sellers on H1 (first studied on
NZDUSD)

In this study I look at the relationship between human desire and
action: belief and the fight. I use the Goodman Box to mark the border
of the fight between buyers and sellers. Volume shows how much liquidity
each side has to support its fight. Time shows whether the fight runs
quickly or very slowly, and either can kill buyers or sellers. In the
end price action tells us honestly what happens inside the war.

Let us start: H1, first studied on NZDUSD and shown here on real
GBPUSD data.

Figure: The chart with no drawing: the conflict cannot be read yet.
Real data: GBPUSD, 1-hour, 15 to 25 February 2022. (The original chart
was NZDUSD 1-hour, August 2021; this one shows the same structure.)

Without any drawing, no one can read the conflict in this chart. That
is why we must connect with the market and touch the sellers' mind and
the buyers' mind. Then we decide which side has more intensity and is
eager to take the flag of domination. Both sides want to be king of the
kingdom.

I start from the top of the chart and go down, following the market.
I do not look at anything on the higher timeframe. Let us read those
minds.

First box: the oasis is an
illusion

Figure: The first box: buyers ride price upward and everything looks
healthy. Real data: GBPUSD, 1-hour, 15 to 25 February 2022. (The
original chart was NZDUSD 1-hour, August 2021; this one shows the same
structure.)

Buyers ride the horse upward and everything looks healthy. But what
we see on the chart is noise. This move is not as promising as it looks.
It looks as if buyers are healthy and one can buy. This oasis is just an
illusion, part of the noise. The volume tells the story behind this
upswing.

Figure: The first box with numbered volume points 1 to 5; the volume
at the top of the box does not fit the size of its bars. Real data:
GBPUSD, 1-hour, 15 to 25 February 2022. (The original chart was NZDUSD
1-hour, August 2021; this one shows the same structure.)

1. Point 1 is the beginning point of the box.

2. At 2 buyers begin to control the land; then for several hours the market moves sideways.

3. At 3 volume rises, but relative to the size of the bar it is fine; no problem.

4. At 4 the size of the bar does not fit the volume, at the end of the bar.

5. A few hours later, at 5, the market moves down on falling volume.

Why does such volume appear at the top of the box? New traders,
sellers, have arrived from different levels of the market. My question
is: does this new army add to the sellers' power or to the buyers'?
Which side does it want to help?

As a guideline: when volume spikes at the end of a box, most of the
time the new army wants to help the opposite force. At 5 the market
moves down by itself, like a gun already loaded with a bullet, the
volume. Volume helps us see that this box holds a new army, so be
cautious.

The new seller army and
the red mark

Figure: "Alert: new seller army" on the first box; the next box shows
sellers taking the market, and a red mark above the first box. Real
data: GBPUSD, 1-hour, 15 to 25 February 2022. (The original chart was
NZDUSD 1-hour, August 2021; this one shows the same structure.)

The new box shows sellers taking the market after the new seller army
at 3 and 4. At 6, again at the end of a box, there is an announcement: a
new buyer army wants to fight the sellers who came at 3.

I put a red mark above the first box. It tests the army's power, its
desire. If the buyers are truly strong, they must move up to that red
level to meet the 1-2-3 requirement. At 7, after the new buyer army, the
market stays silent for a while. The next box is the time to fight. We
will watch which army dies first at the apex of the battle.
The sellers' army camp

Figure: A sharp up box shows eager buyers, but sellers enter in force
at 8 and 9. Real data: GBPUSD, 1-hour, 15 to 25 February 2022. (The
original chart was NZDUSD 1-hour, August 2021; this one shows the same
structure.)

The new box, with its sharp angle, shows buyers eager to control the
kingdom. But the sellers' army has another opinion: at 9 they enter in
force to stop the buyers' progress.

Look at 8: volume and bar are relatively good. At 9 the bar is small.
That confirms our reading: buyers cannot move quickly because of the new
seller army at 8 and 9. It may also confirm that the buyers die before
completing the 1-2-3 cycle. So from 1 to 9 I call it the sellers' army
camp. Notice how volume rises at the top of each box.

Figure: "Sellers' army force camp": at A new buyers enter near the
apex, and at B buyers rise without volume. Real data: GBPUSD, 1-hour, 15
to 25 February 2022. (The original chart was NZDUSD 1-hour, August 2021;
this one shows the same structure.)

In the new box the chart moves to the apex. At A, new traders think
the market will go up. These new traders are bad players, as B confirms.
On the up move at B, after the buyers have failed many times before,
there is no rise in volume.

The message: buyers are losing their power. They cannot fight; they
are old in the battle.
The tiny box: go short

Figure: A tiny box near the apex with very low volume at C: a sell
signal. Real data: GBPUSD, 1-hour, 15 to 25 February 2022. (The original
chart was NZDUSD 1-hour, August 2021; this one shows the same
structure.)

This box is tiny, and it is a sell signal. A tiny box shows buyers
losing power while sellers easily control the market. Look at the volume
at C: sellers control the market easily against so few buyers.

Think about it. Sellers controlled the market against many buyers at
3, 5, 8 and A. Here it is a piece of cake for sellers to push the market
down. That is why the box is tiny. When volume is very small and the
range is small too, that is the confirmation.
The message: buyers are very weak. Go short.
New speed for sellers

Figure: At XX buyers lose energy faster than expected; the new down
box has the sharpest angle so far, with a volume rise at D. Real data:
GBPUSD, 1-hour, 15 to 25 February 2022. (The original chart was NZDUSD
1-hour, August 2021; this one shows the same structure.)

At XX buyers lose their energy faster than expected. The new angle
gives sellers excellent progress. At D volume increases, which suggests
some traders then exit the market, taking profit.

The new angle is clearly the sharpest of all the previous boxes. Now
there is no doubt about the trend: the sellers control the kingdom.
The continuation box

Figure: A continuation box with the TP marked: the bounce at E stops
under the TP. Real data: GBPUSD, 1-hour, 15 to 25 February 2022. (The
original chart was NZDUSD 1-hour, August 2021; this one shows the same
structure.)

This box acts as a continuation box. There is always some volatility
inside a trend, such as E, which closes inside the box and can confuse
traders about the down move. But with the box we are safe. Look how the
buyers stop under the TP.

Volume at C was very, very low, showing that buyers had no interest
in the move at E. The volume at C relative to the size of bar C is good.
So it is confirmed: buyers are too weak to support the market. We move
our stop order to around the TP level. Always protect your gain and kill
your loss.

Figure: The next down box: a volume spike at F mid-box, and more
volume at G at the end of the box. Real data: GBPUSD, 1-hour, 15 to 25
February 2022. (The original chart was NZDUSD 1-hour, August 2021; this
one shows the same structure.)

At F there is a volume spike, but no worry; it is in the middle of
the box. At G volume rises again, and the close of the last bar shows
some strength. It suggests the market is preparing for the next rally.
This angle is slower than the last down box. Still, there is no sign of
an uptrend yet; the crown is still with the sellers' force.
New buyers arrive

Figure: "Alert": at H new traders enter, with volume rising on the up
bars. Real data: GBPUSD, 1-hour, 15 to 25 February 2022. (The original
chart was NZDUSD 1-hour, August 2021; this one shows the same
structure.)

At H new traders enter the market as a contingency. The amount of
buying rises persistently with every up bar. We have not seen that habit
since the downtrend began at the apex. So here we move the stop order
above that rally, and we prepare for an uptrend.

Figure: The slowest down box, with no gain and lower volume at J.
Real data: GBPUSD, 1-hour, 15 to 25 February 2022. (The original chart
was NZDUSD 1-hour, August 2021; this one shows the same structure.)

The angle of this box is the slowest of all, with no gain. It
suggests the sellers are losing their force. For the first time, volume
at J is falling: no new sellers at this level. At H we had many new
buyers. Here we move the stop order.

The message: a new buyer army has arrived, while the sellers give up
or move away. Prepare for an uptrend.

The buyers' army camp and
the Dagger

Figure: "Buyers' army force camp": volume rises on the up move at L
compared with J. Real data: GBPUSD, 1-hour, 15 to 25 February 2022. (The
original chart was NZDUSD 1-hour, August 2021; this one shows the same

Here the buyers' army lives, and the sellers give up. It is easy to

A beautiful Dagger. Can you see that the last down box is tiny? Its

Observe the Market Behavior
(2022)

In this short paper I use one chart (originally AUDUSD daily, redrawn
here on real EURUSD 2-hour data with the same structure) to show how
Goodman Wave Theory reveals the way one swing intersects with other
swings. I borrow two ideas from physics, external force and Newton's
first law, to explain why a swing changes speed or direction exactly
where it meets an earlier structure.

Figure: A down 1-2-3 (FPS, SS, SPS) whose SS stalls near the TP of
the earlier swing, and whose SPS ends in a box past the end of line AA,
the 3C. Real data: EURUSD, 2-hour, 21 February to 4 March 2022. (The
original chart was AUDUSD daily, April to October 2022; this one shows
the same structure.)

Why did the SS fail
to attract more buyers?

"Experiments have thoroughly verified that any change in velocity (speed or direction) must be caused by an external force. The idea of generally applicable or universal laws is important not only here—it is a basic feature of all laws of physics."

The same applies in the market. An external force is the cause, and
its effect is a change in speed or direction.

On this chart it is clear. The SS failed to attract buyers when it
intersected with the TP. The TP acted as a Probability Cause. It
produced the effect of an external selling force that changed the
velocity of the SS.
How far will the SPS run?
"A body at rest remains at rest, or, if in motion, remains in motion at a constant velocity unless acted on by a net external force." — Newton's First Law

Selling will keep dominating price until it intersects with a
Probability Cause, such as the end of line AA, where the 3C principle
comes into play. Watch the box: the price bars start closing at the top.
That change in direction reflects the external force coming from the
Probability Cause, the 3C. The price structure that follows will be
complex or flat.

Figure: The Probability Cause as an external force: a swing keeps its
velocity until it meets a TP or the 3C line, then changes speed or
direction.
The Goodman trader's habit

The Goodman trader always watches these Probability Cause points.
They are an important step in observing market behavior, and in making
an inductive inference about what comes next.

Using
GWT as an Identification Tool for Intermarket Analysis (2025)

This study looks for relationships between currency markets. A topic
like this can easily lead to analysis paralysis, where you end up
nowhere. So I begin with a clear definition of trend, and then I use GWT
to identify how each market stands against that definition.

A working definition of
trend

There are many definitions of trend. The one I find closest to the
reality of the market is this:
A price trend remains dominated by the Propagation until it is cancelled by another Strong Intersection.

This definition holds an inverse relationship between two forces: the
Propagation and the Intersection. The Intersection plays the key role in
halting the Propagation.

Figure: The working definition of trend read top-down, with the
Propagation running until a Strong Intersection halts or cancels it.

(first read on USDMXN, 2-hour)

the others), the stronger the tendency toward a reversal. Likewise, more

stop their Propagation higher. That in turn supports a reversal in

revolving between them. One market becomes the leader, and the others
become laggards.

Markets in Relation,
Revisited (2025–2026)

In 2025 I used Goodman Wave Theory as an identification tool between
markets: a trend is Propagation in control until a strong Intersection
cancels it, and that definition let me compare EURUSD and GBPUSD against
USDCAD and USDMXN. This chapter is what came after. My view of how
markets relate has become simpler, and more careful. A relationship
between two charts is not a rule. It is one more witness.
A witness, not a rule

I never trusted the easy correlation tables. Two pairs that moved
together last month can split apart next week. What I look for is not
the number between them but the process inside each one. On 2024-06-10 I
wrote about how a plan forms:
"Two kind of process meets in one directions. Or works all together in one time . Sellers from diffrent Matrices."

That is the heart of it. When sellers appear in different Matrices of
one chart, the read gets stronger. When the same kind of process appears
in a related market at the same time, it gets stronger again. The other
market does not tell me what to do. It confirms, or it warns.
Looking at the other pairs

Most days I do not watch one chart. I watch a small family. On
2025-07-18 I described what happens when one chart changes my mind:
"Ideas change by overlay deduction. Sometime i see a re propagation. But look other pairs oh this is a nice intersections and count."

One pair shows a re-Propagation, so the trend looks alive. But in the
sister pairs I find Intersections and a 3-C count. That does not cancel
my chart. It makes me patient. If the family is turning, the pair that
still propagates is often the last to turn, not the exception.

My watch notes from 2026 read like this. On 2026-02-02: "here i watch
cadchf / usdcad MO." On 2026-09-08, a longer list:
"NZDCAD is the same as EURCAD, but I prefer EURCAD. … GBPAUD is the best so far. It has an outward overlay."

Two pairs can tell the same story. When they do, I do not trade both.
I choose the cleaner one, the one with the Outward overlay or the better
whitespace. Sister charts are for choosing, not for doubling.
One leads, another lags

On 2026-06-05 I wrote, almost in passing, that things move "like
currency . one leads while another lag". This is what I mean, and the
plate below shows it with real data.

Figure: EURUSD, GBPUSD and AUDUSD on 1-hour closes, each as % change
from 14 Feb 2022. They share one dollar and move together hour to hour,
yet EUR was already the weakest before the 24 Feb shock and finished
three weeks down 3.8%, while AUD finished up 3.3%. (Real data: 1-minute
bars resampled to 1 hour, 14 Feb – 4 Mar 2022.)

Look at what the data says. Hour by hour, the three pairs are
strongly related: the correlation of their hourly moves is between 0.68
and 0.76. Anyone who stops there will say they are "the same trade". But
over three weeks they went in different directions. From 16 Feb, EURUSD
stayed under the zero line while GBPUSD and AUDUSD rose. By 23 Feb, EUR
was down 0.5%, the pound was down 0.1% and the Aussie was up 1.3%. EUR
was the weakest before the shock day, and after it, EUR led the fall.
GBP followed more slowly. AUD dipped with the others for one day, then
went its own way.

So a high correlation does not mean the same direction. It means the
same dollar. The difference between the pairs is the difference between
the other currencies, and that is where the information is. The weak one
leads when the dollar is bought; the strong one resists. When I look for
a short, I want the leader. When I look for the end of a move, I watch
the lagger: if the lagger finally makes its Intersection, the family is
turning.
Consensus across the family

The 2025 study ended with a rule I still use: the more Intersections
across the group, the stronger the tendency toward reversal. Since then
I add a second test. Before I accept a market story, I ask the chart to
approve it. On 2025-10-10, watching gold, I wrote:
"This also must approve it by the chart. A nice setup in 1 hour will approve this assumption."

News, fear, a strong dollar, a weak euro: these are only assumptions.
The relationship becomes useful when it shows up as structure, a 1-2-3,
a Propagation, an Intersection, a count. If the story is true, the setup
appears. If no setup appears, I keep the story to myself.
Relation as a money question

The newest idea is that relationships between markets belong to money
management, not only to analysis. On 2025-08-30 I wrote:
"Flat jumbo + setup . Is less risky than a propagation jumbo with a setup."
and a few lines later:
"Each setup may play a rule . Maybe for a more gains . Or a hedge , or a decrease the risk."

When I hold more than one trade, they are not separate. Two trades in
different Market Environments can balance each other. Two trades in the
same environment, on the same currency, are one trade with double
size.

That is why, in 2026, I built the danger into my trading expert as a
guard. Layer 9 of the Poka-Yoke system, which I described to Michael on
2026-09-17, is the Correlated Exposure Barrier: it "Automatically
detects if two open trades are compounding your risk on the same
currency (e.g., holding EURUSD and GBPUSD simultaneously)." Look again
at the plate. Long EURUSD and long GBPUSD in that February would not
have been two trades. They would have been one bet against the dollar,
lost twice.
And for the record

Relationships also matter in how I measure. On 2025-01-30 I wrote
that my sample of trades must not be bent by them: "The most important
they are not correlation different time". If ten trades in my series of
thirty are really one dollar move, my Golden Ratios lie to me. The
record must hold independent samples, each with an equal chance, or it
is only a story I tell myself.
What I keep

• A relationship between markets is a witness, not a rule. The chart must approve it.

  • High correlation means the same base, not the same direction. The information is in the split.

  • Among sister pairs, I trade the cleanest one, never all of them.

  • The weak one leads; the lagger tells me when the family has turned.

  • Two trades on the same currency are one trade. My expert blocks it, and my record should not count it twice.

Rung 4 · Deciding:
Goodman's Tools and the Setup
The tools I use to read a chart, and how I decide whether what I see deserves my money.
The Goodman Box (2021)

In this study I use the Goodman Box for entering and exiting a trade,
and also as an independent Overlay. I add nothing to this core. The core
by itself is a full trading system.

The idea: think in the
frame of the 1-2-3

The Goodman Box is simple. Instead of thinking in the 1-2-3, we think
in the frame of the 1-2-3. We frame every 1-2-3, and then we deal only
with its two edges: the EP-SPS at the top and the BP-FPS at the
bottom.

So this study deals with every frame that contains a 1-2-3. Once the
1-2-3 is framed, we forget about it and concentrate our mind on the
frame alone: EP-SPS and BP-FPS.

Figure: A 1-2-3 framed by a box, read only at its upper edge (EP-SPS)
and lower edge (BP-FPS), with the terms Excess, TP and TEST.

At this beginning stage I study only these relationships. I will not
go further into angle, time or volume. I only want to show how to
interpret boxes within a market context. In Goodman we know the market
moves by 1-2-3s. So our job here is to deal only with the EP-SPS and
BP-FPS of each 1-2-3. This is important.
Two terms:

• When price moves back to the BP-FPS, we call it a TEST.

  • When price moves to (and beyond) the EP-SPS, we call it an Excess.

Fitting the market with
boxes

Every 1-2-3 can be framed. But I want to frame it in a way that
interprets the price action. I do not want to draw a thousand boxes
without trying to understand the message behind the chart.

The market is like a musical composition. A box can explain its
symbols, so that a trader can read the music. This requires skill and
science.

Figure: The raw chart before any box is drawn: a strong rally, a long
sideways range, then new highs. Real data: AUDUSD, 1-hour, 24 Feb – 4
Mar 2022. (The original chart was of an unnamed symbol and period; this
one shows the same structure.)
Box 1 and the red mark
Let us draw the first box.

Figure: The first box framing the opening rally, with a red mark at
its top edge where the buyers showed their maximum power. Real data:
AUDUSD, 1-hour, 24 Feb – 4 Mar 2022. (The original chart was of an
unnamed symbol and period; this one shows the same structure.)

I add a red mark at the top of the box. It tells very clearly that
the buyers showed their maximum power here. After that, the sellers
control the trend with another box. Whenever this happens, I suggest
drawing a new box that shows the sellers' power.
The Tipping Point

Next I add a TP to the box. When the next box cannot move below the
50% point, it suggests Propagation of the 1-2-3 upward.

Figure: Box 1 with its 50% TP marked in black; the next box holds
well above it. Real data: AUDUSD, 1-hour, 24 Feb – 4 Mar 2022. (The
original chart was of an unnamed symbol and period; this one shows the
same structure.)

The black line represents the 50% TP. Holding above it shows a
stronger tendency to complete the direction of Box 1.
Box 2: the Return Zone box
Now let us draw Box 2.

Figure: Box 2, the Return Zone box, with two TESTs of its lower edge.
Real data: AUDUSD, 1-hour, 24 Feb – 4 Mar 2022. (The original chart was
of an unnamed symbol and period; this one shows the same structure.)

I call this a Return Zone box. It promises a move into a new 1-2-3.
We also have the 6&6 box, which represents a reversal box.

As I said, we do not care about anything inside the box. We look only
at the boundary. So there is no Setup inside the box, only outside
it.

When the market makes an Excess above the Return box, we cancel the

As shown here, I remove the red mark and replace it with a green one

The new box carries a red mark. It shows the buyers losing power,

When the market then moves to a new high, as in the next chart, we

The Goodman Box with Time
(2021)

The time element reveals a great deal about the next direction. Time
shows whether buyers move fast or slow, how long they take to reach
their maximum, and when they are losing power. So time tells us when the
buyers are at the end of their movement. In this study I add time to the
Goodman Box and discuss it with charts.
What we measure

With time in the Goodman Box, we deal only with the distance between
two or three EP-SPS, between two or three BP-FPS, and with the breakout
points.

Figure: Δ EP, the time buyers take to travel from one EP-SPS to the
next.

Δ EP shows the time the buyers take to arrive at the second
EP-SPS:

• Small delta: the buyers are very fast.

  • Large delta: the buyers take a long time, so their power is decreasing.

  • Normal delta (compared with the other deltas): no alarm.

That is all we need to study time relationships. The market can only
move up or down, but time can show which of the two is stronger. Time
shows how the buyers lose their power, bit by bit.

In this study I will not look at the inverse relationship, the time
from BP-FPS to EP-SPS. I leave that advantage aside, because it deals
with box angles.

A first example: boxes A, B and
C

Figure: The chart before the boxes are drawn: a fall, a fast rally, a
slower second fall back toward the low, then a strong rise. Real data:
USDCHF, 1-hour, 21–24 Feb 2022. (The original chart was USDCHF daily;
this one shows the same structure on the same symbol, in the window the
data covers.)
Let us draw the Goodman Boxes and try to interpret them.

Figure: Boxes A, B and C, with the new speed of Box B and Δ BP, the
time between the bottoms of A and C. Here Box B runs slightly above the
top of Box A, and Box C stops 18 pips above the bottom of Box A. Real
data: USDCHF, 1-hour, 21–24 Feb 2022. (The original chart was USDCHF
daily; this one shows the same structure on the same symbol, in the
window the data covers.)

Box A creates an Ending Point. Then Box B shows a great new speed
from the buyers, reaching a point very close to the top of Box A. This
alarms us. Buyers are fast and sellers are fast too, so we simply wait
to see which one becomes slower.

Box C arrives at the same Ending Point as Box A, but its delta is
relatively slow. The gains of Box C show that buyers are stronger than
sellers. This can be a 6&6 box.
To summarize:

1. The buyers moved above the TP of Box A with new speed. That says the buyers are stronger.

2. Box C then moved slowly and reversed inside the box several times. That shows the sellers losing their power.

This type of 6&6 box can also solve a 6&6 flat, by using
time.

If you are still not convinced by this example, there is much more.
When we study time, we need more data to reach the best confidence in a
trade. Do not force a trade. If you still have no confidence, follow
your heart, not the trade, especially with time.

A long study: reading
time at TP, EP and BP

Let us study this chart without looking for a Setup, only to
understand some time phenomena. I study price action only at the TP, EP
or BP.

Points 1 to 4: sellers
cannot push down

At 1, the Ending Point, price runs to the TP. At 2 we have a delta:
the buyers take a lot of time, forming a minor 6&6. At 3 there is a
reversal bar at the TP, but this box shows a new buyer speed that
reaches the TP. Then the market moves down to the level of 1, at 4.

Figure: The zone from 1 to 4 where sellers fail to move price lower.
Real data: EURUSD, 1-hour, 16 Feb – 1 Mar 2022. (The original chart was
USDCHF daily. USDCHF data now exists, but only for 14 February – 4 March

From 1 to 4 we see a zone where the sellers cannot move down. Why?
The buyers' move from 1 to 2 shows a new habit that forces the sellers
to reduce their power. At 4 there is a buy Setup: a 6&6.

Points 5 and 6:
buyers lose power at the TP

Look at the time between 5 and 6. The market is facing sellers, and

After 6, I call this whole zone the sellers' area. The sellers camp

Goodman Overlay (2021)

In this paper I show how an Overlay is built up, step by step, until
it gives me real strength when I take a position. I start from a watch
chart, qualify the setup with inside charts, and only then go outside to
confirm.

Figure: Tracking runs along the watch chart over time; qualifying
goes deep into one candidate setup.
The two questions
Two questions sit at the heart of the Goodman method:

1. What do I see now?

2. What do I want to see next?
We have three basic outside overlays:

• Matrix Overlay

  • Propagation Overlay

  • Nest

Figure: The two questions repeat at every step, checked against the
three outside overlays.

The watch chart: USDCAD
4-hour

First I define the watch chart, the chart I use to find a setup. Then
I play with the inside charts and the outside charts. My watch chart is
USDCAD, 4-hour. The charts below redraw the same structure on real
EURUSD data. The volume readings at each numbered point come from my
original USDCAD point and figure chart, so the redrawn volume columns
will not match every reading.

Figure: The watch chart: the Jumbo down, then the range where the
Setup is tracked. Real data: EURUSD, 1-hour, 23 Feb – 1 Mar 2022. (The
original chart was USDCAD 4-hour, August 2021; this one shows the same
structure.)

What do I see now? There is a potential 6&6. As Goodman said,
"Setup is Setup to go." Whenever it works, it should give me a 1-2-3
up.

Figure: The potential 6&6 on the watch chart, with its target and
maximum risk marked. Real data: EURUSD, 1-hour, 23 Feb – 1 Mar 2022.
(The original chart was USDCAD 4-hour, August 2021; this one shows the
same structure.)

What I like in a Goodman Setup is that the risk is always limited,
while the profit is almost double, to the TTL. That is why trading
Goodman setups is so profitable.

Which Matrix is dominant, and why? Before I go outside and confuse
myself, I want to qualify the setup. I will use a point and figure
chart.

Qualifying with
point and figure and volume

Why did the PTS or
Goldilocks fail?

Figure: The point and figure chart with volume per column, marking
points 1 to 3 and asking why the PTS failed. Real data: EURUSD point and
figure from 5-minute closes, box 0.0004 (4 pips), 3-box reversal, 24 Feb
– 1 Mar 2022. (The original chart was a USDCAD point and figure chart,
August 2021; this one shows the same structure. The volume readings in
the text describe the original chart.)

• At 1: there is a large amount of sales. Buyers agree and take it, so new buyers absorb all the offers.

  • At 2: the market is in the Return Zone. The amount of sales shows many new buyers entering here. But can those buyers support the market? Is there any pulling force?

  • At 3: the market moves up with no change of property. There is no amount of sales in the volume, so no new buyers can support the market.

For the market to move up, it needs new buyers, or at least no
sellers who can push it down. So the market moved down to test its
Matrix Overlay, the FMX.

This shows clearly why the market always follows the Nash
equilibrium. Participants always look for maximum profit. At 3 the
buyers sat at a very low Nash point; no one wanted such a move. Buyers
want a lot of profit, so the market moved down to test.

Measuring the energy at the
test

Figure: Points 4 and 5 compared with the energy at A. Real data:
EURUSD point and figure from 5-minute closes, box 0.0004 (4 pips), 3-box
reversal, 24 Feb – 1 Mar 2022. (The original chart was a USDCAD point
and figure chart, August 2021; this one shows the same structure. The
volume readings in the text describe the original chart.)

• At 4: the market dips a little to test the MO, and no new sellers respond. Sellers have no passion to move it down. Compare the shift of energy from A to 4: at A there was a lot of energy to move it down.

  • At 5: new buyers arrive with a very good Nash equilibrium, as we see when we measure that energy. The amount of sales at 5 is about the same as at 2, but the buyers' response here is more effective, with more energy than at the PTS. That is why the 6&6 succeeded.

We must look for a more energetic response, where just a little
energy gives a lot of momentum compared with before.

Figure: Points 6, 7 and 8, where low volume comes with upward
momentum. Real data: EURUSD point and figure from 5-minute closes, box
0.0004 (4 pips), 3-box reversal, 24 Feb – 1 Mar 2022. (The original
chart was a USDCAD point and figure chart, August 2021; this one shows
the same structure. The volume readings in the text describe the
original chart.)

• At 6: no new sellers, a very low amount, no change of property, at a very critical point with a very low Nash equilibrium. Sellers are weak.

  • At 7: a great difference. Just a small amount of sales gives a great momentum. When the market gives a very small amount with a greater Nash and momentum, it shows the passion to move up. They are happy.

  • At 8: this amount of sales suggests no new sellers. The volume is far lower than anywhere before, and the Nash equilibrium is very small.

What do I want to see next? A 1-2-3. Let us watch how buyers play
with the PO Overlay at the next TP.

The Propagation Overlay and
its TP

Figure: Point 9, where new sellers enter near the 50% TP of the
Propagation Overlay. Real data: EURUSD point and figure from 5-minute
closes, box 0.0004 (4 pips), 3-box reversal, 24 Feb – 1 Mar 2022. (The
original chart was a USDCAD point and figure chart, August 2021; this
one shows the same structure. The volume readings in the text describe
the original chart.)

At 9: what do I see now? Because of the Propagation Overlay we have a TP at 50%. Sellers who think the market will move down enter here, so we see new sellers at 9, with a new Nash. But this should not exceed the 1-2-3. The 1-2-3 will act as a magnet for those sellers and stop their flow before BP-PTS.

What do I want to see next? The flow of orders from new sellers must
withdraw before BP-PTS.

Figure: Points 10 and 11, where the sellers' flow dries up into a
nested 6&6. Real data: EURUSD point and figure from 5-minute closes,
box 0.0004 (4 pips), 3-box reversal, 24 Feb – 1 Mar 2022. (The original
chart was a USDCAD point and figure chart, August 2021; this one shows
the same structure. The volume readings in the text describe the
original chart.)

• At 10: there is a good new seller, as the amount of sales shows.

  • At 11: no new sellers, with a very small amount of sales. This is a nested 6&6 case. The Nash equilibrium is very low. Compare 11 with 10 and 9. The 1-2-3 acts like a magnetic field that keeps sales from entering the market.
What do I want to see next? New energy to the upside.

A nested 6&6 inside a
bigger Overlay

Figure: A nested 6&6 inside the bigger Overlay, with point 12
touching the TP. Real data: EURUSD point and figure from 5-minute
closes, box 0.0004 (4 pips), 3-box reversal, 24 Feb – 1 Mar 2022. (The
original chart was a USDCAD point and figure chart, August 2021; this
one shows the same structure. The volume readings in the text describe
the original chart.)

As the cycle shows, there is a nested 6&6 in the PTS with a
bigger 6&6 Overlay. There is a lot in this chart.

At 12: a very small amount of sales produces a very large Nash equilibrium that touches the TP. The mass behaviour is happier with the uptrend Matrix than with the downtrend Matrix. It is very obvious: the dominant passion is up.

What do I want to see next? A 1-2-3, or no great response to the
TP.

Figure: Point 13 and the Dagger, a 3S Setup where new sellers fail to
push the market lower. Real data: EURUSD point and figure from 5-minute
closes, box 0.0004 (4 pips), 3-box reversal, 24 Feb – 1 Mar 2022. (The
original chart was a USDCAD point and figure chart, August 2021; this
one shows the same structure. The volume readings in the text describe
the original chart.)

Here we go. At 13: new sellers appear, but without great energy. Look at the red arrow: before the market touched the TP, it generated new energy with a good Nash point. Now, at 13, new sellers come in without any success in generating more downward movement. Compare the amount of sales at 13 with 9.

So here is a 3S Setup, as the Dagger shows. The last up move, X, came
on a very low amount, which shows some happy passion in the mass
behaviour.
What do I want to see next? A breakout of the upper Dagger line.

Confirming with the outside
Overlay

Then I go to the outside Overlay to check what can support this
study. I also want to confirm the 3S count: the outside count should
approve the watch chart count. Again, there is a lot here.

Figure: The outside chart, where the market is still in its old
slope. Real data: EURUSD, 4-hour, 14 Feb – 1 Mar 2022. (The original
chart was USDCAD daily, 2021, with a target box confirming the watch
chart; this one shows the old slope only.)
Thank you.
Overlay Combination (2021)

In this study I want to show exactly how an Overlay combination
affects two things: risk and reward. A strong combination may promise a
safe trade; a weak one increases the risk. In the second part I build
the combination on a logical basis and show four combinations of
extremes that I trade.
Too many choices

In any market in the world there is at least one product or service
to attract buyers. But with so many products, so much innovation and
technology, the consumer faces many types of one item. There are lots of
competitors.

When you want to buy a phone, you face Apple, Samsung, Huawei and
others. Even within one company there are many models and sizes. I read
some new sales books saying the best strategy is to give the customer
only three choices.

Today's stock market is no different. I find software that searches
for patterns in more than 30,000 stocks around the world. That is just
more rope for traders to hang themselves.

It is easy to get emotional about a stock and rush to buy something
you know nothing about. This behaviour must be avoided. What looks like
an opportunity is not always a real opportunity.

In Goodman theory we start from the general and move to the specific.
Very few people want to look at things from a deep angle. The real
opportunity is in the details, deeper and more specific.
The equation of every market

Every market has an equation, simple mathematics. I buy any amount of
something at X, then I sell it at Y:

1. Y < X: I paid more than I sold for. I am a loser.

2. Y = X: a waste of time, but I can try again.

3. Y > X: I am a winner.

There is no fourth case in any transaction. We are all obedient to
this equation.

Figure: The three outcomes of every trade and the basic requirement
of Y > 2X.

If you keep taking losses, you will soon damage yourself. That is why
the market is so dangerous. Goodman put the Overlay there to help us
avoid losing trades, not always, but most of the time. You can stay in
the market for a long time by making at least breakeven or enough
profit.
Two words to avoid
Two ideas must be avoided when we deal with the market:

1. Always. There is always someone smarter than you who wants to take your money.

2. Guarantee. There is no guarantee the market will follow your words.

The market lives on another planet. The market is the BIG BOSS. Facts
sometimes become strange, but in the end they are facts.

There is an advantage too. Once you start, you will never find peace
in stopping, because you know there is only a small distance to your
next dream. And there is extra news: "Compound interest is the eighth
wonder of the world. He who understands it earns it … he who doesn't …
pays it." (Albert Einstein)
Who loses?

Again, simple logic. At the end of any deal, the future shows who is
the loser and who is the winner:

• Losers are those who buy and the price moves down.

  • Losers are those who sell and the price moves up.

In both cases Y < X. Successful trading means buying something
that at least promises you can sell it higher. Otherwise you are the
loser.

There is risk in every minute in the market. "No Risk No Reward"
(Goodman). The risk is buying a stock you cannot sell higher, where Y
< X. That is why we want to know which trade can promise at least Y =
X. But the excellent trade is when we sell at more than twice, and
above. Better still is trading the Line.
So we must always look at:

1. The risk of the trade: X.

2. The potential profit: Y > X.

3. At least Y > 2X.

Take a trade only when there is a real potential of Y > 2X. That
is the basic requirement for every trade.
Why the combination matters

An Overlay combination with a Goodman Setup helps us find that
requirement. Every combination with any Setup directly affects risk and
reward. A bad combination may hurt both. Trading with not enough
Overlay, or with a weak Overlay, causes greater risk.

From this point I must give a caution. You need judgement and
experience, which come from trading for months and years, until
judgement becomes a sixth sense. Then you can become an excellent
picker.

The logic behind a
combination

• Strongly bullish combination: buyers can pull the market up. The trend is dominated by happy passion and controlled by greed. The real reward is with buyers, at least Y > 2X, and it is less risky to trade.

  • Strongly bearish combination: sellers dominate and can pull the market down, controlled by fear. The real reward is with sellers, at least Y > 2X, and you can go short safely.

There are specific degrees between strongly bullish, bullish and even
neutral. Each degree can produce Y > X, Y < X or Y = X. Recording
this is very important for feedback and for building a library.

The Goodman process:
the market is a movie

The Goodman process is an ability to connect with the market
emotionally. In Goodman, the market is a movie. The movie shows changes
of passion from extreme sadness to extreme happiness.

The Overlay combination is the checking part of the movie. When the
market shows one of the Goodman setups, a Setup is set up to go. The
combination shows the forces from different parts of the movie that say:
yes, this setup can go. Each scene tells us the change in passion, up or
down.

In brief, each Overlay is one scene; the combination is the full
movie, from the start to the current price. We aim to find the
combination that fits each market. Every market is unique. There is no
duplicate movie.
Justice versus expectation

The Overlay combination aims to do justice to each buyer and seller
according to their ability to give me Y > X. "There is not enough
overlay" (Goodman). This means we still cannot do justice to buyers or
sellers: we cannot say whether they can make the setup go.

Every trader wants to expect, or guess, that a trade will be
profitable. Very soon they find themselves in conflict with their own
feelings. A guess is not strong evidence that can give us confidence.
Imagine a court of law judging someone by a guess.
Proactive reading

In every scene the market shows us how it works with the Overlay,
from smaller Overlays in the lower time frame to the larger scene in the
higher time frame. Read the Overlay by using Propagation. To do justice
to an Overlay, we must look at how the Overlays are interconnected.

A weak combination:
the daily and the 4-hour

Suppose we have a 6&6 in a 4-hour chart and want to trade it
against the daily chart, where we have a Matrix Overlay.

Figure: A possible 4-hour 6&6 against a daily Matrix Overlay back
at its origin point without a 3-C.

Does this Overlay promise me Y > 2X? Let us do justice to it. On
the daily chart, ask: is there any cancellation, a 3-C? If not, we
cannot assume this point is the end. There are still sellers.

So I will not take this 6&6. The setup can fail, because the
market has more energy to break down than to move up. Some will say,
"Double bottom, let's buy!" But bigger investors will dump the market by
increasing their selling force.

Here is an example. The higher time frame (the daily in my
original):

Figure: The higher time frame has fallen back to its prior low with
no 3-C, so sellers are still in control and a bounce here is weak. Real
data: EURJPY, 1-hour, 18 Feb – 2 Mar 2022. (The original chart was
USDZAR daily, late November 2020; this one shows the same
structure.)
The lower time frame (the 4-hour in my original):

Figure: On the lower time frame a base forms on the low line and
lifts, which looks like a possible buy. Real data: EURJPY, 15-minute,
1–2 Mar 2022. (The original chart was USDZAR 4-hour, late November 2020;
this one shows the same structure.)

Can this combination give us a good Line? I do not think so. It shows
the market is too weak for buyers to carry it up.

Figure: The rally from the base was sold and price broke to new lows:
a weak combination with no Overlay behind it. Real data: EURJPY, 1-hour,
28 Feb – 4 Mar 2022. (The original chart was USDZAR 4-hour, late
November 2020; this one shows the same structure.)

Then the market moved to new lows. Why? Very simply, the market did
not have enough Overlay. The bigger investors on the daily chart dumped
every up move; they saw the 4-hour rally as an opportunity to sell more.
This example shows how a bad combination increases the risk.
Knowledge versus wisdom

What is the difference between what we know and what we learn?
Knowledge can be found everywhere. Fitting that knowledge to serve our
aims and purpose is a pearl of wisdom.

A campaign in trading means looking deeply at every Goodman point,
using the Goodman process, to output one of three decisions: Long, Short
or Don't Trade.
Anatomy of a campaign

Instead of thinking of one trade, think of 10 trades as one campaign.
No one can rely on one trade.

1. Operation. Always look out for trades (Tracking), to find candidates for the 10-trade campaign.

2. Strategy. Before entering, make sure there is a logical ability that can make the setup go (Staging): identify the Overlays for a possible trade.

3. Technique. The trader's skills after deciding to enter: where to put the stop-loss, when to raise the stop order, when to take profit.

4. Feedback. Was the campaign successful: Y < X, Y > X or Y = X? What was the most important element that made it succeed or fail? The more questions, the better. Learn from losses and wins.

Figure: The four stages of a ten-trade campaign and its three
possible decisions.

In brief, each campaign has two things: buy now and sell later. When
you sell later, the result is Y < X, Y > X or Y = X.

On the next pages I show 5 trades as part of a campaign, and also
some trades I avoided because there was not enough Overlay. Each uses a
1-hour Setup with a 1-day Overlay. Remember, the aim of every campaign
is 10, 4, 1.

Chart 1: first traded on
TRYJPY, 1-hour

Figure: The chart before any boxes are drawn: first read which force
is greater. Real data: AUDUSD, 30-minute, 23–25 Feb 2022. (The original
chart was TRYJPY 1-hour; this one shows the same structure.)

Is this trade Y > X, Y < X or Y = X, and why? What do I see
now? I want to read the real force: which is greater, buyers or
sellers?

Figure: The Jumbo box A with a volume surge at its end, then the
small box B, where late sellers have no future. Real data: AUDUSD,
30-minute, 23–25 Feb 2022. (The original chart was TRYJPY 1-hour; this
one shows the same structure.)

We have two boxes. The range A is a Jumbo. But look at the end: the
volume increased abnormally, meaning many transactions took place there.
What is the future for that amount of sales?

Remember: at the end of any deal, the future shows who is the loser.
Losers are those who buy and the price moves down, and those who sell
and the price moves up. In both cases Y < X.

At B there is no future for those who sold the market late. The
market is now dominated by buyers; the reward is with buyers. Can you
see there is no reward with sellers at B? In the middle of box B the
volume increased, but the future belonged to buyers. Look at the range
of B: do you want that kind of profit?

The lesson: be cautious when volume increases at the end of a box and
the next box is a small range.

Figure: Points 1 and 2 after box B, asking whether the next one is a
3 and where the reward is. Real data: AUDUSD, 30-minute, 23–28 Feb 2022.
(The original chart was TRYJPY 1-hour; this one shows the same

Is the next one a 3? And where is the possible reward?

Figure: The PTS setup from 2: the reward points back to the top of A,
the risk sits below box B. Real data: AUDUSD, 30-minute, 23–28 Feb 2022.
(The original chart was TRYJPY 1-hour; this one shows the same

A runaway count. For maximum profit, one can take the Line. This

Where is the problem? Instead of going up to 3, it moved down to B.
Let us go to the higher time frame (the daily in my original).

Figure: After 1 and 2, price stores energy between the excess line

What do I see now? The current price is between the test and the
excess lines, storing energy, near the bottom of Matrix Overlay point 2.
Let us judge the market:

1. The market moves between the excess and test lines, storing energy for a new move.

2. The market is very near the bottom at 2.

3. We have a Jumbo with a PTS on the 1-hour.

4. It is newly bullish on the daily (very near the bottom) and on the 1-hour.

5. We still do not know when the market can break out of the excess line.

6. The market is non-trending on the daily, but the 1-hour shows an uptrend.

7. There is still no 1-2-3 on the daily chart.

8. The market environment (ME) shows very low directionality and very low volatility.

The problem is: can it break out of the excess line, or will it move
sideways? This trade is Y = X, 5 of 10 risky, because the daily is
non-trending and storing energy. Looking at buyers, though, they can
stop the downward movement on the daily, so it is still bullish. If
someone pushed me to enter, I would enter a buy only.

But one must enter only the best trades. This one is risky for me, so
I will pass. I do not want to enter between excess and test. I trade a
1-hour chart, so I do not want to be stuck in a very slow move.

EURCAD, 1-hour

I want to point out the angle. The first angle shows the force of the

In this chart there is:

2. More than 12 bars at the energy level.

This case must be supported by a daily setup, some of the Nested

I also want to see how the mass is attracted at each of A, B and

• At 1: with the SPS, the amount of sales increased, suggesting they want to move it higher.

  • At 2: at the Return Zone, also the beginning of the apex, the volume increased more than at 1. Buyers again want to move it up.

  • At 3: the market moves up with almost no energy. The fight with sellers is very weak, so it moves up easily.

  • At 4: the same as 1 at A. Buyers want to enter again; they see the reward up.

  • At 5: the market moves down to take all the stop-losses there. The volume increased very quickly, but instead of pushing lower, it gave a very strong close at 5. Buyers dominate the trend.

In brief, the mass enjoys the uptrend more than the downtrend. When
the market moves up on increased volume, as at A and B, it shows bullish
passion. Sellers try to stop that passion, but 5 shows there are no more
sellers.

Now the higher time frame (the daily in my original), to see the
movie. What do I see now? The daily chart holds many important things
that support the 1-hour story.

of stored energy, a Goldilocks, then the Return Zone. Real data: GBPJPY,
1-hour, 21 Feb – 2 Mar 2022. (The original chart was EURCAD daily; this
one shows the same structure.)

The market is at the end of the SPS of a Goldilocks, in the Return
Zone. The daily chart shows a 6&6, then weeks of energy, then
confirmation with a Goldilocks. It is very interesting. Sometimes the
trend takes a very long time, with many patterns, as it tries to
reverse.

In brief, an Overlay combination must be a logical combination that
shows the real force behind buyers or sellers. As these charts show,
with a strong combination the trader many times gets an excellent
reward, often the runaway count. In the end, you have the right to
choose what is best for you. Do not let any chart force you to trade.
"Sit on your hands" (Goodman).

Part 2: How to
construct a logical combination

Instead of using guesses, expectations or tips, a logical combination
can set up and promise a very good return. But first: what do we mean by
trading?

Trading as an engineering
balance

In engineering, a balance is kept on a conserved quantity (money,
energy, total mass) in a system. The system can be a single process
unit, like buying and selling a stock, or an entire process, like a
campaign:
Input + Generation − Output − Consumption = Accumulation

• Input: what enters through the system boundaries.

  • Generation: what is produced within the system.

  • Output: what leaves through the system boundaries.

  • Consumption: what is consumed within the system.

  • Accumulation: what builds up within the system.

For example, every 3 months a trader puts 10,000 USD into trading
(input). He loses 2,000 USD (consumption), wins 8,000 USD (generation),
and takes 5,000 USD home (output). So 10,000 + 8,000 − 5,000 − 2,000 =
11,000 USD accumulated after 3 months.

The real risk in trading is when the market cannot generate any
profit (generation), or consumes a lot of your money (consumption). Both
happen within the system, the process unit. So trading is just a
machine: a trading vehicle. In engineering, anything lost within the
system is called consumption. When a vehicle consumes more money than it
generates, it must be fixed.

From this, trading is 100% safe when you choose the best vehicle, one
that generates more than it consumes. When you start from a logical
basis, you easily know what you want. The Goodman process helps you
understand which vehicle suits you. The Overlay combination must sit
within the system, to make sure it can generate more than it
consumes.

Four logical combinations
of extremes

I found 4 logical combinations that show the most extreme points,
where Y (generation) > X (consumption). When they occur, they give a
buy or sell signal:
1. Sell signal: extreme happiness on the daily chart and extreme happiness on the 1-hour chart.

• Daily: 6&6, Goldilocks, Dagger; better when it occurs at an MO or PO.

  • 1-hour: 6&6, Goldilocks, Dagger.
2. Buy signal: extreme sadness on the daily and extreme sadness on the 1-hour. "When there's blood in the streets, you buy."

• Daily: 6&6, Goldilocks, Dagger; better at an MO or PO.

  • 1-hour: 6&6, Goldilocks, Dagger.
3. Buy signal: the daily is at the beginning of happiness, or very far from extremes, and the 1-hour shows extreme sadness.

• Daily: PTS; better at an MO or PO.

  • 1-hour: 6&6, Goldilocks, Dagger.
4. Sell signal: the daily is at the beginning of sadness, or very far from extremes, and the 1-hour shows extreme happiness.

• Daily: PTS; better at an MO or PO.

  • 1-hour: 6&6, Goldilocks, Dagger.

Figure: The four daily/1-hour combinations that give a signal;
anything else gives none.

My job is to qualify the Overlay. When the market is not in one of
these cases, there is no signal. I trade only extremes, as a type of
Nested Overlay, with the MO and PO supporting the Nested Overlay.
